title: Ten minutes a day
intro: A short magazine-style article about a woman who learned Spanish in small steps. It was written for Psotek English; Marta is a made-up example.
paras: When Marta, a nurse from Gdańsk, decided to learn Spanish at the age of forty-two, her friends were not exactly encouraging. "You work night shifts," one of them reminded her. "When exactly are you going to study?" Marta didn't have an answer. She only knew that she had always wanted to read Spanish novels in the original, and that she was tired of waiting for the perfect moment.

Her solution was almost embarrassingly simple: ten minutes a day, every day, no matter what. On busy days she listened to a short podcast on the bus. On quiet days she wrote three sentences in a notebook about what she had done. She never allowed herself to skip a day, but she also never forced herself to do more than ten minutes. "If I felt like continuing, I continued," she says. "But the promise was only ten minutes. That made it impossible to say no."

At first, progress was slow. After three months she could order food and ask for directions, but she still froze whenever someone answered her quickly. The turning point came in the second year, when she found an online conversation partner in Valencia who wanted to practise Polish. They met on video twice a week, spending half an hour in each language. Mistakes, she discovered, were not a disaster. "My partner made as many mistakes in Polish as I did in Spanish. We laughed a lot, and that took the fear away."

Three years later, Marta is reading her fourth Spanish novel. She admits that she still uses a dictionary and that her grammar is far from perfect. However, she believes the small daily habit taught her something more valuable than any language rule. "Big goals scare us," she says. "Small ones don't. Ten minutes doesn't sound like much, but ten minutes every day for three years is more than a hundred and eighty hours."

Her advice to other adult learners is simple: choose a time that is so small you cannot fail, attach it to something you already do every day, and find someone to talk to as soon as possible. "Don't wait until you are ready," she says. "Nobody ever feels ready."
